theorems.title: Resolution-Handoff Continuity Theorem — fixed Bandwidth
theorems.statement: If Resolution handoff commutes, presentations share retained Formal Identity, the Identity Witness remains valid, and merged essential distinctions remain recoverable through provenance, then non-injective coarsening is structurally continuous under the declared contract.
theorems.conclusion: coarsening may change distinguishability without erasing canonical structure

theorems.title: Bandwidth Modifier Resolution-Descent Condition
theorems.statement: A typed Bandwidth modifier M descends to a well-defined Resolution readout map only if source Resolution equivalence is respected by the target readout: a~_R b implies M(a)~_R' M(b).
theorems.conclusion: induced readout map exists iff equivalence is respected

theorems.title: Recovery Witness Fiber-Separation Theorem
theorems.statement: Let F_c be the fine-lineage fiber over one coarse Resolution handoff/readout c, and let W be the retained recovery-witness map on F_c. A witness-mediated recovery selector returns a unique declared fine lineage for every element of F_c if and only if W separates distinct recovery-relevant lineages on F_c (equivalently: W restricted to F_c has no collisions under the declared structural equivalence).
assumptions: non-injective handoff fiber F_c is declared
selector may use only retained witness data and may not invent suppressed structure
theorems.conclusion: Unique lineage recovery is equivalent to fiber separation by the retained witness; non-separating witness bundles are insufficient without an additional discriminator.
